one_liner: Nim task- and data-parallel runtime that uses message-passing work-requesting; claims 3-10x less scheduling overhead than TBB and GCC OpenMP.
what_it_does: Weave is a multithreading runtime for Nim with one worker per logical core. Its API is spawn/sync futures (Flowvar) for task parallelism, nestable parallelFor/parallelForStrided/parallelForStaged loops with explicit captures, parallel reductions, dataflow tasks triggered by FlowEvents, and an experimental background-service mode where foreign threads submit jobs. It is a Nim library compiled through Nim's C or C++ backend, not a C++ API, so it does not drop in for TBB, OpenMP or Cilk.
how_it_is_fast: It follows Andreas Prell's Tasking 2.0 design: idle workers send steal requests over SPSC/MPSC channels and busy workers answer them (work-requesting), instead of thieves touching shared Chase-Lev deques. Thieves adapt between steal-one and steal-half, loops are split lazily only when a steal request arrives (adaptive lazy loop splitting, no grain size), and task memory comes from a thread-local pool with a lookaside buffer modelled on mimalloc/snmalloc, with lock-free batching MPSC channels. Optional lazy Flowvar allocation (-d:WV_LazyFlowvar) cuts overhead by at least 2x more on very fine-grained tasks, per the README.
when_to_use: Nim programs with very fine-grained recursive parallelism (fib, DFS, nqueens style trees) where TBB-like runtimes need about 10,000 cycles per task to break even; Weave targets tasks from about 2,000 cycles
Nested parallel loops where you do not want to tune grain size or partitioning (lazy splitting handles it)
Dataflow or pipeline graphs expressed with FlowEvents on top of the same scheduler
Research or teaching on message-passing schedulers, or targets without good atomics (the design only needs channels)
when_not_to_use: C++ codebases: there is no C++ API; you would have to write the parallel code in Nim
Nim 2.x: open issues #201 (task compilation fails for Nim >= 2.0.0, type mismatch on gcsafe), #200 (README examples do not compile) and #171 (recent Nim makes Weave crash)
Code that blocks or sleeps inside tasks: scheduling is cooperative, so a blocked worker starves steal requests and others spin

Production systems that need proven correctness: README marks it experimental, only one of two complex sync primitives was formally verified, and there are open livelock/deadlock bugs (#130 parallelFor livelock, #149 syncScope stall, #161 background submits go missing)
GC-managed Nim types in tasks: not tested; pass raw pointers instead

integration.dependencies: Nim stdlib plus the synthesis nimble package
integration.min_toolchain: Nim >= 1.2.0 (nimble); broken on Nim >= 2.0.0 per issue #201
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows on x86, x86-64, ARM64 (CI-tested with C and C++ backends); any pthread target; Windows 32-bit needs MSVC, not MinGW
integration.thread_safety: Tasks spawned only from Weave worker threads; foreign threads must use setupSubmitterThread/submit/waitFor (experimental)

gotchas: Forgetting init(Weave)/exit(Weave) gives nil pointer exceptions on spawn
With -d:WV_LazyFlowvar, Flowvars must be at most machine-word size and cannot be returned, or you hit stack smashing or crashes
syncScope does not compile in C++ backend mode inside a for loop (Nim issue 14118); awaitable loops are not barriers for grandchildren tasks
benchmarks/README lists histogram and logsumexp parallel reductions as pathological cases with a suspected bug in parallel reductions
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Weave only if you write Nim and want TBB/Cilk-class task parallelism with dataflow tasks; for C++ work, Staccato and Nowa compare against TBB/Cilk with published numbers, and Fork Union covers low-overhead parallel-for.
verified_claims_summary: Only the README headline was found: 'as low as 3x to 10x less overhead than Intel TBB and GCC OpenMP on overhead-bound benchmarks', backed by a public benchmark suite (fibonacci, DFS, nqueens, heat, matmul, BPC, SPC, ...) but no result tables, compiler versions or CPU models in the repo pages read.
status_note: Stale since 2023-12-09 with open compile failures on Nim 2.x; MIT or Apache-2.0, useful mainly as a Nim library or a reference design for work-requesting schedulers.
